definition: In robot learning, a vision–language–action model (VLA) is a class of multimodal foundation models that integrates vision, language and actions.
details: Given an input image (or video) of the robot's surroundings and a text instruction, a VLA directly outputs low-level robot actions that can be executed to accomplish the requested task. VLAs are generally constructed by fine-tuning a vision-language model (VLM) (i.e. a large language model extended with vision capabilities) on a large-scale dataset that pairs visual observation and language instructions with robot trajectories. These models combine a vision-language encoder (vision transformer), which translates an image observation and a natural language description into a distribution within a latent space, with an action decoder that transforms this representation into continuous output actions, directly executable on the robot. The concept was pioneered in July 2023 by Google DeepMind with RT-2, a VLM adapted for end-to-end manipulation tasks, capable of unifying perception, reasoning and control.

explainer.lead: A vision–language–action model is a class of multimodal foundation model that integrates vision, language and actions. It matters because it lets a robot turn an image of its surroundings plus a text instruction directly into executable low-level actions.

tiers.eli5: You show the robot a picture of what it sees and tell it what to do in words, and it produces the actual movements to do it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build VLAs by fine-tuning a vision-language model on large-scale data pairing visual observations and language instructions with robot trajectories. A pitfall is that the model depends on the coverage and scale of that paired trajectory data.
tiers.paperLevel: A VLA takes an input image or video of the robot's surroundings and a text instruction and directly outputs low-level robot actions. It is generally constructed by fine-tuning a VLM on a large-scale dataset pairing visual observation and language instructions with robot trajectories, combining a vision-language encoder such as a vision transformer with other components.

explainer.example: Given a camera image and the instruction to perform a task, the VLA outputs the low-level actions that accomplish it.
